messages:
zara: Drafting a PRD/RFC for private-deploy networking. Focus: customer-managed egress, dual-stack IPv4/IPv6 support, split-horizon DNS for control plane, and safe fallback behavior when customer blocks outbound. Posting initial scope and acceptance bullets here — ping @choi @ben for infra/security items. Link to draft: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/privnet-ipv6-dns-draft

choi: thanks. can you enumerate acceptance criteria and the hard failure modes we need to handle?

zara: sure, early list — will expand in PRD.
- Acceptance: customers can bring static egress IPs (BYO-EIP) OR opt into Redwood SNAT.
- Acceptance: if customer requests IPv6, the connector + control plane must negotiate IPv6 and fall back to IPv4-only without request failure.
- Acceptance: split-horizon DNS: control plane queries must resolve internal service names to private IPs when routed over customer network; public DNS must remain unchanged.
- Acceptance: control plane must produce explicit audit logs for every egress decision (timestamp, route, reason).
- Acceptance: rollout gating requires 3 successful customer e2e validations (one IPv6-first, one IPv4-only, one mixed NAT64 scenario).
- Hard failure modes: customer blocks outbound 443; customer blocks ICMP/PMTU causing MTU issues; asymmetric routing causing TLS handshake pinholes. Define graceful degradation: route to hosted fallback model if customer opts in, otherwise fail fast with clear error and operator alert.

ben: add security requirement: mTLS for connector<->control-plane, with automatic cert rotation and revocation list handling. Also need proof that egress IP binding cannot be spoofed by tenant.

maya: edge case: customers on NAT64-only environments (no native v6) — need UTs and a compatibility matrix. Also DNS64 interactions with split-horizon could be funky. Put DNS team on-review.

product-liz: for prioritization: this is customer-driven by Acme and two other accounts. What are proposed launch criteria and timeline?

zara: proposed launch gating:
1) PRD + RFC reviewed by infra/security/DNS (OK).
2) E2E automated tests + 3 customer validation runs pass.
3) Performance check: control-plane handshake p99 increase <= 50ms under expected load.
4) Rollout playbook + rollback tested in staging.
5) Security review and threat-model sign-off.
Target: Q2 milestone if reviews and customer test windows align.

devon: testing notes: include chaos tests for intermittent link flaps, and an MTU/fragmentation test harness. Add synthetic traffic that simulates large embedding payloads.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: CI pipeline triggered for branch privnet/ipv6-dns (build 236. Running e2e smoke).

zara: noted — will add acceptance test matrix to doc. Also adding a small config snippet for customer templates: 
```
customer_network:
  egress_mode: [byo-eip | redwood-snat]
  ipv6: [enabled | disabled | prefer]
  dns: split_horizon: true
  fallback: hosted_failover: [opt-in | opt-out]
```

choi: +1. also include observability: tokens/calls routed via customer network must show route tag in console and cost/latency breakdown.

ben: flag for rollout: onprem connector upgrade may require kernel/network driver patches for jumbo frames in some customer environments. Document compatibility matrix and fallback to MSS clamping.

maya: i'll add DNS engineers to reviewers and schedule a deep-dive on Monday.

product-liz: sounds good — I'll slot this in the roadmap as 'high priority' for Q2 given revenue signal. Please ensure we have a clear rollback and customer communication template.

zara: will convert RFC into a PRD with an acceptance table and rollout checklist. Thanks all — please review the draft linked above, comments by Tue end.

ben: will review security section ASAP.

choi: will create a short staging test plan and paste links in the doc.

ops-bot: incident-bot: new issue created: PRIVNET-1023 "e2e test: NAT64 compatibility" assigned to maya.
